newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Canadian firm shows interest in Zambia's Konkola.
newsitem.headline: Canadian firm shows interest in Zambia's Konkola.

text.p: The Zambian Privatisation Agency said on Tuesday that a Canadian mining house had expressed interest in joining a consortium to develop Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines' (ZCCM) Konkola Deep Mine.
Privatisation agency chief Valentine Chitalu said that the company, which he declined to name, was keen to replace Australia's Western Mining Corp.
Earlier this year Western Mining pulled out of the consortium led by Anglo American Corp of South Africa.
"Anglo have proceeded with negotiations with a Canadian mining company on the development on Konkola. I cannot tell you which company it is until negotiations have been completed," Chitalu said.
He said that Western Mining pulled out of the consortium because it considered the project "too large a commitment to make in Africa".

"People overseas have very negative views about Africa and are cautious about investing here. On the other hand, we consider the privatisation of ZCCM a very serious matter. We do not want to sell it only to have it collapse," he said.
The Anglo consortium, which includes the giant mining house Gencor Ltd, opened talks with the Zambian government on Konkola in January this year.
The two sides were expected to sign a memorandum of understanding by May, but have not yet done so.
"The memorandum of understanding has not yet been signed because all decisions relating to ZCCM are very complex," Chitalu said.
He said that the delay in signing the memorandum of understanding had delayed the commencement of a nine months feasibility study by Anglo into the project.

Some analysts say the Anglo consortium and other mining houses are reluctant to commit themselves to large investments in Zambia until presidential and parliamentary elections are held by the end of October.
The run-up to the elections has been marked by increasing political tensions, culminating in the emergence of underground groups and a western donor freeze.
The devlopment of Konkola is seen as crucial to the future of Zambia's copper mining industry.
